newsitem.title: GERMANY: Clashes halt Berlin rightwingers' jobs demo-police.
newsitem.headline: Clashes halt Berlin rightwingers' jobs demo-police.

text.p: Several people were injured on Saturday when right-wing youths on their way to a protest meeting to "keep jobs for the Germans" clashed with left-wing groups in Berlin, German police said.
About 50 rightists and skinheads had to turn back to a suburban train station in Hellersdorf in eastern Berlin shortly after they arrived there.

Police said left-wing groups, including the members of the federation of Jewish students, the German DGB trade union federation, the reform communist PDS party and Turkish groups organised a counter-demonstration.
Chanting "Nazis out" some of the leftwingers surrounded the rightists and skinheads, threw stones at them and drove them back into the station.
Some rightists holding flags with the colours of the old German empire hid inside a train standing at the station, while leftwingers tried to prise the doors open.
German riot police turned up in several vans. They broke up the clashes and detained several people.
Medical workers treated some youths who had blood running down their faces.
Police did not yet know how many were injured or detained.

The clashes are a sign of growing social unrest amid soaring unemployment and warnings from trade unions that jobless figures which hit a new post-war low of 4.66 million in January could get even worse.
